title: Holi, Namaste and Helping Others
bigQuestion: How can we be kind to people and to every living thing?

story.title: Colors in the Air
story.kicker: Pink and green powder fills the air, and two old friends laugh and hug.
paragraphs: It is spring. The sun is warm again. Children run into the park with bags of colored powder. Pink, green, yellow and blue.
Arjun sees his friend Meera across the grass. Last week they had a fight. They did not talk for days. Arjun feels a little shy.
Meera smiles. She tosses a puff of pink powder at him. Arjun laughs. He tosses green powder back. Soon they are both covered in color.
"Happy Holi!" they shout. They hug. Many families say Holi is a day to make up with friends. Arjun and Meera are friends again.
story.think: Arjun and Meera made up. What helps you make up with a friend?

lessons.title: A Spring Festival
lessons.mainIdea: Holi is a happy spring festival of colors.
reading: *Holi* is a festival of colors. It comes in the spring, in March in many years. It welcomes the warm days.
People throw colored powder. They spray colored water. They sing and dance. They share sweets and food.

look.title: A Rainbow Crowd
look.text: Look at the people in the street. Their white shirts are now pink, green and blue. Their faces are yellow and purple. Everyone is laughing.
look.prompt: Name three colors you see in this picture.

check.q: What is Holi?
check.why: Holi is the spring festival of colors.

check.q: When is Holi?
check.why: Holi comes in the spring.

check.q: What do people throw at Holi?
check.why: People throw colored powder at Holi.

lessons.title: Making Up With Friends
lessons.mainIdea: Many families say Holi is a time to make up and start fresh.
reading: At Holi, everyone is covered in color. You cannot tell who is who! Many families say this helps people feel equal.
Many say Holi is a time to forgive. Friends make up after fights. Neighbors share food. It is a fresh start.

words.d: to stop being angry with someone

look.title: A Fresh Start
look.text: Look at two neighbors. Last year they argued about a fence. Today one brings the other a plate of sweets. "Happy Holi," she says. The other one smiles.
look.prompt: Why is a festival a good time to make up?

check.q: What do many say Holi is a time to do?
check.why: Many families say Holi is a time to forgive.

check.q: What does forgive mean?
choices: To stop being angry with someone
check.why: To forgive is to stop being angry.

check.q: Why can't you tell who is who at Holi?
check.why: At Holi, color covers everyone.

lessons.title: The Boy Who Stayed Brave
lessons.mainIdea: Prahlada stayed brave and kind, even when it was hard.
reading: Prahlada was a prince. He loved Vishnu with all his heart. Many Hindus honor Vishnu as God.
His father was a proud king. He wanted everyone to honor only him. Prahlada said no, kindly. He kept loving Vishnu. He stayed brave.

words.d: a boy in the stories who stays brave and loyal to Vishnu
honored by many Hindus as God who protects the world

look.title: Prahlada Stays True
look.text: Prahlada's father tries many times to make him stop honoring Vishnu. Each time Prahlada stays calm and true, and each time he is kept safe.
look.cite: Retold from the Bhagavata Purana, Book 7, chapters 5 to 8
look.prompt: How does Prahlada act when his father is angry?

check.q: Who did Prahlada love with all his heart?
check.why: The Bhagavata Purana says Prahlada loved Vishnu.

check.q: What did Prahlada's father want?
check.why: His proud father wanted to be honored above all.

check.q: How did Prahlada act?
check.why: Prahlada stayed brave and kind.

lessons.title: The Bonfire
lessons.mainIdea: Many people light a bonfire the night before Holi to remember Prahlada.
reading: In a well-known Holi story, Prahlada is kept safe from a great fire. His cruel aunt Holika is not.
So the night before Holi, many people light a big bonfire. They remember that Prahlada was kept safe. They say good wins over bad.

look.title: Around the Fire
look.text: Look at the families around the bonfire. It is night. The fire crackles. The grown-ups keep the children at a safe distance. They tell the story of Prahlada.
look.prompt: Why do families tell a story around the fire?

check.q: When do many people light the Holi bonfire?
check.why: Many light a bonfire the night before Holi.

check.q: Who is kept safe in the story?
check.why: In the Holi story, Prahlada is kept safe.

check.q: What do people say the bonfire shows?
choices: Fire is fun to play with
check.why: Many say the bonfire shows good winning over bad.

lessons.title: Namaste
lessons.mainIdea: Namaste is a greeting with hands pressed together.
reading: *Namaste* is a greeting. You press your hands together. You bow your head a little. Many Hindus greet people this way.
Many explain namaste as honoring the good in the other person. It is a kind, gentle way to say hello.

words.d: a greeting with hands pressed together and a small bow

look.title: Saying Hello
look.text: Look at the grandpa at the door. A guest arrives. The grandpa presses his hands together. He bows a little. "Namaste," he says. The guest does the same.
look.prompt: What are different ways people say hello? Name two.

check.q: What is namaste?
check.why: Namaste is a greeting with hands together.

check.q: How do people hold their hands for namaste?
check.why: For namaste, people press their hands together.

check.q: How do many explain namaste?
choices: Honoring the good in the other person
check.why: Many explain namaste as honoring the good in others.

lessons.title: Ahimsa: Not Hurting
lessons.mainIdea: Ahimsa means not hurting any living thing.
reading: *Ahimsa* is an old word. It means not hurting. Not hurting people. Not hurting animals. Not hurting any living thing.
Many Hindus, Jains and Buddhists teach ahimsa. Some families eat no meat because of it. Mahatma Gandhi made ahimsa famous.

look.title: A Great Duty
look.text: The Mahabharata calls not hurting others the highest duty.
look.cite: Retold from the Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva (Book 13)
look.prompt: What does this old book say is the highest duty?

check.q: What does ahimsa mean?
check.why: Ahimsa means not hurting any living thing.

check.q: Who made ahimsa famous?
check.why: Mahatma Gandhi made ahimsa famous around the world.

check.q: Why do some families eat no meat?
check.why: Some families eat no meat to follow ahimsa.

lessons.title: Seva: Helping Others
lessons.mainIdea: Seva means helping others without asking for anything back.
reading: *Seva* means helping others. You help without asking for a reward. Many Hindus and Sikhs do seva.
Some cook and serve free meals at a temple. Some clean a park. Some help a neighbor. Every helper counts, like the little squirrel.

words.d: helping others without asking for anything back

look.title: Ways to Help
look.cite: Common forms of seva described by Hindu and Sikh communities
look.prompt: Which way to help could you do this week?

check.q: What is seva?
choices: Helping others without asking for a reward
check.why: Seva means helping others freely.

check.q: Where do some people serve free meals?
check.why: Some people serve free meals at a temple as seva.

check.q: Which story also shows that every helper counts?
check.why: The squirrel story shows every helper counts.

review.why: Holi is the spring festival of colors.

review.q: Who stayed brave and loved Vishnu?
review.why: Prahlada stayed brave and loved Vishnu.
Namaste is a greeting with hands pressed together.
Seva means helping others without asking for anything back.

review.q: What do many say Holi is a time to do?
review.why: Many say Holi is a time to forgive and make up.
